plugins.name: Pyright
plugins.description: Microsoft's Python type checker and language server.

settings.label: Python Interpreter
settings.description: The interpreter whose installed packages Pyright resolves imports from. The default is the workspace's own .venv; when there is none, Pyright uses the Python on your PATH.

settings.label: Type Checking
settings.description: How strictly Pyright checks types: Off reports only syntax and import errors, Strict everything it can.

settings.label: Errors and Warnings
settings.description: Which files Pyright checks for the Error List: the files you have open, or every file in the workspace, open or not.

settings.label: Auto-Import Suggestions
settings.description: Suggest names from modules the file does not import yet, adding the import when one is chosen.

plugins.name: ty
plugins.description: Astral's Rust-built Python type checker and language server. An alternative to Pyright.

settings.label: Errors and Warnings
settings.description: Which files ty checks for the Error List: the files you have open, or every file in the workspace, open or not. ty reads this only when it starts, so changing it restarts the server.

settings.label: Variable Types
settings.description: Show the type ty infers for a variable that does not name one, after its name. ty reads this only when it starts, so changing it restarts the server.

settings.label: Parameter Names
settings.description: Show the name of the parameter each argument is passed to, before the argument. ty reads this only when it starts, so changing it restarts the server.

settings.label: Auto-Import Suggestions
settings.description: Suggest names from modules the file does not import yet, adding the import when one is chosen. ty reads this only when it starts, so changing it restarts the server.

plugins.name: Lua Language Server
plugins.description: Lua language support, from the sumneko project.

settings.label: Inlay Hints
settings.description: Show the server's hints in the code: parameter names, and the types of locals and returns.

settings.label: Check Lua
settings.description: Report syntax errors, undefined globals and the like in the Error List.

plugins.name: sqls
plugins.description: SQL language support: completion, formatting and query execution.
plugins.detail: Configure a database connection to get schema-aware completion.

plugins.name: Perl Navigator
plugins.description: Perl language support: diagnostics, completion and navigation.

plugins.name: Dockerfile Language Server
plugins.description: Rapid7's Dockerfile linting, completion and hover support.

plugins.name: YAML Language Server
plugins.description: Red Hat's YAML validation, completion and schema support.

settings.label: Formatting
settings.description: Let Format Document and Format Selection lay out YAML files.

settings.label: Check YAML
settings.description: Report syntax errors, and values a file's schema does not allow.

settings.label: Schemas From SchemaStore
settings.description: Match well-known files, such as GitHub workflows and Compose files, to their schemas from schemastore.org, which needs the network.

plugins.name: Bash Language Server
plugins.description: Shell script completion, linting and documentation on hover.

plugins.name: Svelte Language Server
plugins.description: Svelte component diagnostics, completion and navigation.

settings.label: Parameter Names
settings.description: In a component's TypeScript, show the name of the parameter each argument is passed to, before the argument: for literal arguments only, or for all of them.

settings.label: Variable Types
settings.description: In a component's TypeScript, show the type the compiler infers for a variable that does not name one.

settings.label: Return Types
settings.description: In a component's TypeScript, show the return type the compiler infers for a function that does not name one.

settings.label: Parameter Types
settings.description: In a component's TypeScript, show the type the compiler infers for a parameter that does not name one, such as in a callback.

settings.label: Property Types
settings.description: In a component's TypeScript, show the type the compiler infers for a class property that does not name one.

plugins.name: HTML, CSS & JSON Language Servers
plugins.description: Microsoft's web language servers, extracted from VS Code.

settings.label: Check styles
settings.description: Report syntax errors and unknown properties in style blocks and style attributes.

settings.label: Check scripts
settings.description: Report syntax errors in script blocks.

settings.label: Check CSS
settings.description: Report syntax errors and unknown properties in CSS files.

settings.label: Check SCSS
settings.description: Report syntax errors and unknown properties in SCSS files.

settings.label: Check Less
settings.description: Report syntax errors and unknown properties in Less files.

settings.label: Check JSON
settings.description: Report syntax errors, and values a file's schema does not allow.

settings.label: Check certificates
settings.description: Refuse a server whose certificate is not trusted when downloading a JSON schema.

plugins.name: rust-analyzer
plugins.description: Rust language support.
plugins.detail: Runs cargo to load a workspace, so the Rust toolchain must be on your PATH.

settings.label: Check on Save
settings.description: Run Cargo over the workspace each time a file is saved, and show what it reports beside the server's own diagnostics.

settings.label: Check Command
settings.description: The Cargo command run on save. Clippy needs the clippy component of the toolchain.

settings.label: Variable Types
settings.description: Show the type the compiler infers for a variable that does not name one.

settings.label: Parameter Names
settings.description: Show the name of the parameter each argument is passed to, before the argument.

settings.label: Method Chain Types
settings.description: Show the type at each step of a method chain that spans several lines.

settings.label: Closing Brace Names
settings.description: Show what a long block belongs to after its closing brace.

settings.label: Elided Lifetimes
settings.description: Show the lifetimes the compiler fills in on a function's signature.

settings.label: Closure Return Types
settings.description: Show the return type the compiler infers for a closure.

settings.label: Binding Modes
settings.description: Show the references and dereferences a pattern match adds by itself.

settings.label: Implicit Reborrows
settings.description: Show where the compiler reborrows a reference by itself.

settings.label: Implicit Drops
settings.description: Show where values are dropped at the end of their scope.

settings.label: Enum Discriminants
settings.description: Show the value of each enum variant.

settings.label: Code Lenses
settings.description: Show lenses above items: running them, and how often they are used.

settings.label: Run Lenses
settings.description: Show Run above a main function, and Run Test above a test.

settings.label: Implementation Counts
settings.description: Show how many implementations a trait, struct or enum has above it; clicking the count lists them.

settings.label: Reference Counts on Types
settings.description: Show how many references a struct, enum or union has above it; clicking the count lists them.

settings.label: Reference Counts on Methods
settings.description: Show how many references a method has above it; clicking the count lists them.

settings.label: Reference Counts on Traits
settings.description: Show how many references a trait has above it; clicking the count lists them.

settings.label: Reference Counts on Enum Variants
settings.description: Show how many references an enum variant has above it; clicking the count lists them.

settings.label: Symbol Search
settings.description: What Go to Symbol in Workspace searches.

settings.label: Complete Unimported Names
settings.description: Offer names that are not imported yet; accepting one adds its use.

settings.label: Function Call Completion
settings.description: What completing a function or method name adds after it.

settings.label: Import Grouping
settings.description: How imports added by a completion or a code action are merged into the use items already there.

settings.label: Import Paths
settings.description: How the paths of imports added by a completion or a code action start.

settings.label: Server Diagnostics
settings.description: Show the errors the server finds itself as you type, before Cargo has run.

settings.label: Experimental Diagnostics
settings.description: Show diagnostics the server is still working on, which may report code that compiles.

settings.label: No Default Features
settings.description: Analyse every crate without its default Cargo features.

settings.label: Run Build Scripts
settings.description: Run each crate's build script while loading, so the code it generates is understood. Build scripts are programs: they run with your permissions.

settings.label: Expand Procedural Macros
settings.description: Expand procedural macros, so the code they generate is understood. Procedural macros are programs: they run with your permissions.

plugins.name: clangd
plugins.description: C and C++ language support, from the LLVM project.
plugins.detail: A large download — it carries the Clang toolchain headers.

settings.label: clang-tidy Checks
settings.description: Report what clang-tidy finds beside the compiler's own errors. The checks come from the project's .clang-tidy file. The server reads this only when it starts, so changing it restarts it.

settings.label: Insert Includes
settings.description: Add the #include a completion needs when it is accepted. The server reads this only when it starts, so changing it restarts it.

settings.label: Background Index
settings.description: Index the whole project in the background, so references and symbols are found in files that are not open. The server reads this only when it starts, so changing it restarts it.

plugins.name: .NET Debugger (netcoredbg)
plugins.description: Debug .NET projects.
plugins.detail: Samsung’s MIT-licensed .NET debugger. Microsoft’s vsdbg is not offered: it is licensed only for use within the Visual Studio family.

plugins.name: Rust Debugger (CodeLLDB)
plugins.description: Debug Rust programs and tests.
plugins.detail: Vadim Chugunov’s MIT-licensed LLDB front end, with its own LLDB build. On macOS it uses Apple’s debugserver, from Xcode or the Command Line Tools.

plugins.name: Go Debugger (Delve)
plugins.description: Debug Go programs and tests.
plugins.detail: The Go project's own MIT-licensed debugger, spoken to over its DAP server. It builds what it debugs with your Go toolchain, so `go` must be on the PATH. On macOS it uses Apple’s debugserver, from Xcode or the Command Line Tools.

plugins.name: Node Debugger (js-debug)
plugins.description: Debug Node projects with Microsoft's js-debug.
plugins.detail: Platform-independent JavaScript, run under the Node runtime Studio ships.

plugins.name: Python Debugger (debugpy)
plugins.description: Debug Python projects.
plugins.detail: Needs Python 3.8+ on your machine. Ships the pure-Python build, which debugs any interpreter version but steps more slowly than a compiled one.

plugins.name: Native Disassembler
plugins.description: Disassembles native machine code (x86, x64, ARM, ARM64) using Capstone.
plugins.detail: Decodes the machine code inside PE, ELF, Mach-O and MS-DOS binaries. Studio ships no decoder of its own, so this provides the assembly listing the binary editor shows.

plugins.name: JVM Bytecode Decoder
plugins.description: Shows the bytecode inside Java class files, method by method.
plugins.detail: Pure TypeScript, so it needs no JVM installed. Source line numbers appear when the class was compiled with -g.

plugins.name: WebAssembly Decoder
plugins.description: Shows the instructions inside WebAssembly modules, function by function.
plugins.detail: Pure TypeScript, so it needs no toolchain installed.

plugins.name: .NET IL Decoder
plugins.description: Shows the IL inside managed .NET assemblies, method by method.
plugins.detail: Reads ECMA-335 metadata, so it needs the whole assembly rather than the visible range. Needs the .NET runtime installed. Large assemblies are truncated to the first 2000 methods.

plugins.name: Docker
plugins.description: Talk to a Docker-compatible container engine over its local socket.
plugins.detail: Speaks to the engine over its local socket; it does not install or run a container engine itself. Open Shell uses the docker command-line tool when one is installed.

plugins.name: Podman
plugins.description: Talk to a Podman container engine over its local socket.
plugins.detail: Speaks to the engine over its local socket; it does not install or run a container engine itself. Open Shell uses the podman command-line tool when one is installed.

plugins.name: SQLite
plugins.description: Connect the Database Explorer to SQLite database files.
plugins.detail: Opens SQLite database files on this machine with the SQLite built into Studio's own runtime; it installs nothing else.

plugins.name: PostgreSQL
plugins.description: Connect the Database Explorer to PostgreSQL servers.
plugins.detail: Connects to PostgreSQL servers over the network with `pg`, a pure-JavaScript client; it installs no database and no native code.

plugins.name: Neo4j
plugins.description: Connect the Database Explorer to Neo4j graph databases.
plugins.detail: Connects to Neo4j over Bolt with the official JavaScript driver; it installs no database and no native code.

plugins.name: SQL Server
plugins.description: Connect the Database Explorer to SQL Server and Azure SQL.
plugins.detail: Connects to SQL Server and Azure SQL over the network with `tedious`, a pure-JavaScript client; it installs no database and no native code. Splits scripts at GO like SSMS, and shows PRINT and RAISERROR in Messages.

plugins.name: Git
plugins.description: Git version control: status, history, diffs, commits, branches, remotes, tags, stashes, merges, rebases, worktree checkouts, ignore rules and per-file history.
plugins.detail: Drives the git installed on your machine, or one you point it at in Settings. Needs git 2.23 or later.

plugins.name: GitHub
plugins.description: GitHub hosting: pull requests with their checks, issues and comments, Actions runs (re-run and cancel), and your accounts and repositories — and, for you and your agents, opening, editing, labelling and closing issues, linking sub-issues, and opening and editing pull requests.
plugins.detail: Signs in with the GitHub CLI's login (gh auth login), or a token you add in Settings. Serves github.com.

plugins.name: Claude
plugins.description: Runs Claude through Anthropic's Agent SDK in its own process, over Studio's agent protocol.
plugins.detail: The full Claude agent: sessions held open across turns, sub-agents, background tasks, slash commands, per-tool policy, write confinement, the OS sandbox, model discovery, and Remote Control through claude.ai/code. Authenticates with your local `claude` login, or with an Anthropic API key set on the connection. Downloads around 200MB: the SDK ships its Claude Code CLI as a native binary, and one platform's is fetched.

providers.description: Run Claude through your Claude subscription (local login) or an Anthropic API key. Add one configuration per account.

authMethods.hint: Uses your local Claude login (~/.claude) through the Claude Agent SDK.
Uses an Anthropic API key, stored encrypted on this machine.

plugins.name: Codex
plugins.description: Runs OpenAI Codex as an app-server in its own process, over Studio's agent protocol.
plugins.detail: Holds a Codex thread open across turns, so a conversation keeps its context. Streams replies, reasoning, shell commands, file changes and web searches into the transcript, and asks you through Studio's permission card before a command runs or a file changes, under your posture and per-tool settings. Authenticates through your local Codex login, or through an API key configured against the connection.

providers.description: Run OpenAI models through your Codex subscription (local login).

authMethods.hint: Uses your local Codex login (~/.codex) through the OpenAI Codex CLI.

plugins.name: AI SDK
plugins.description: Runs OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Ollama and any OpenAI-compatible endpoint through the Vercel AI SDK, in its own process.
plugins.detail: The general-purpose harness: point a connection at any model API and this runs it. Studio supplies the tools for the turn's surface and runs them on the model's behalf, so an agent on Ollama has the same capabilities as one on Claude. Asks the endpoint what models it offers. Authenticates with the API key configured against the connection; a local Ollama server needs none. Around 2MB — the SDK is pure JavaScript and ships inside the plugin.

providers.description: Run OpenAI models through an OpenAI API key.

authMethods.hint: Uses a OpenAI API key, stored encrypted on this machine.

providers.description: Run Gemini models through a Google AI API key.

authMethods.hint: Uses a Google Gemini API key, stored encrypted on this machine.

providers.description: Run DeepSeek models through a DeepSeek API key.

authMethods.hint: Uses a DeepSeek API key, stored encrypted on this machine.

providers.description: Run Grok models through an xAI API key.

authMethods.hint: Uses a xAI API key, stored encrypted on this machine.

providers.description: Run local models through an Ollama server.

authMethods.hint: Talks to a local Ollama server. No credentials needed.

providers.description: Run any OpenAI-compatible endpoint — a self-hosted gateway, or a provider not listed here.

authMethods.hint: Uses a custom endpoint's API key, stored encrypted on this machine.

plugins.name: npm
plugins.description: npm packages: the projects in a folder, what each declares, what is installed, what is newer, and search across its registries.
plugins.detail: Reads package.json, your lockfile and .npmrc. Installing and updating run through the npm, pnpm or Yarn on your machine, in a terminal you can see.

plugins.name: NuGet
plugins.description: NuGet packages: the .NET projects in a folder, what each references, what is restored, what is newer, and search across its feeds.
plugins.detail: Reads your project files, restore output and nuget.config. Adding and updating run through the dotnet on your machine, in a terminal you can see.

plugins.name: Go modules
plugins.description: Go modules: the modules in a folder or go.work workspace, what each requires, the version selected, what is newer on the module proxy, and lookup of a module by its exact path.
plugins.detail: Reads go.mod, go.work, go.sum and your Go environment (GOPROXY, GOPRIVATE). Adding, updating and removing run through the go on your machine, in a terminal you can see.

plugins.name: vcpkg
plugins.description: vcpkg packages: the C and C++ manifests in a folder, the ports each depends on, the version its baseline resolves, what is newer, and search across the vcpkg port list.
plugins.detail: Reads vcpkg.json and vcpkg-configuration.json, and the vcpkg registry's published baselines. Adding a port and installing run through the vcpkg on your machine, in a terminal you can see.

plugins.name: Conan
plugins.description: Conan packages: the C and C++ conanfiles in a folder, what each requires, what its lockfile resolved, what is newer, and search across its remotes.
plugins.detail: Reads conanfile.txt, conanfile.py (as text, never run), conan.lock and your Conan remotes. Installing runs through the conan on your machine, in a terminal you can see.

plugins.name: Cargo
plugins.description: Cargo crates: the Rust crates and workspaces in a folder, what each depends on, what Cargo.lock resolved, what is newer, and search across crates.io and your registries.
plugins.detail: Reads your Cargo.toml files, Cargo.lock and Cargo's own config and credentials. Adding, updating and removing run through the cargo on your machine, in a terminal you can see.

plugins.name: PyPI
plugins.description: Python packages: the projects in a folder, what each declares, what is locked or installed, what is newer on PyPI or your own index, and exact-name lookup.
plugins.detail: Reads pyproject.toml, requirements files, Pipfile, setup.cfg, your lockfile or virtual environment, and pip.conf. Never runs Python. Changes run through the uv, Poetry, Pipenv or pip on your machine, in a terminal you can see.

plugins.name: Maven and Gradle
plugins.description: JVM packages: the Maven and Gradle projects in a folder, what each declares, what is newer on Maven Central or your own repositories, and search across Maven Central.
plugins.detail: Reads your POMs, Gradle build scripts, version catalog, Gradle lockfiles, ~/.m2/settings.xml and gradle.properties. Neither Maven nor Gradle has a command that adds a dependency, so this plugin only resolves them, through the mvn or gradle on your machine, in a terminal you can see.

plugins.name: .NET Tests
plugins.description: .NET tests in the Tests panel: xUnit, NUnit and MSTest, found in your test projects and run through dotnet test.
plugins.detail: Finds tests by reading your project files and C# sources, without building anything. Running them uses the .NET SDK on your machine, in a terminal you can see.

plugins.name: JavaScript Tests
plugins.description: JavaScript and TypeScript tests: finds what Vitest, Jest and Playwright Test would run, runs them, and reads their results back.
plugins.detail: Reads package.json and your test files to find tests, without running anything. Running them uses the Vitest, Jest or Playwright your project installs, in a terminal you can see.

plugins.name: Python Tests
plugins.description: Python tests: finds what pytest would collect, unittest suites included, runs them, and reads their results back.
plugins.detail: Reads your test files to find tests, without starting Python. Running them uses the project's own virtual environment (.venv or venv) when it has one, else python3, with pytest installed there, in a terminal you can see.

plugins.name: Rust Tests
plugins.description: Rust tests in the Tests panel: finds #[test] functions in each crate and runs them with cargo test.
plugins.detail: Reads your crates' sources to list their tests; running them uses the cargo on your machine, in a terminal you can see.

plugins.name: Go Tests
plugins.description: Go tests in the Tests panel: finds Test and Fuzz functions in each package and runs them with go test.
plugins.detail: Reads your packages' _test.go files to list their tests; running them uses the go on your machine, in a terminal you can see.

plugins.name: JVM Tests
plugins.description: JUnit tests in the Tests panel: finds test classes and methods under src/test and runs them with Gradle or Maven.
plugins.detail: Reads your test sources to list their tests; running them uses your Gradle or Maven wrapper, or the one on your machine, in a terminal you can see.

plugins.name: CTest
plugins.description: C and C++ tests in the Tests panel: lists a CMake build's CTest tests and runs them with ctest.
plugins.detail: Asks ctest which tests a configured build directory declares, which runs none of them; running them uses the ctest on your machine, in a terminal you can see.
